title: One-third adaptive tolerance with an exact global-clock selector

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, put n=ceil(log2 N). Use the single bank-first clock algorithm in proof.md and critical_third_adaptive_clock_selector.md, with Q=192 for N=2 and Q=27648(2n+20) for N>=3, r=Q/3, t=n+18, J=n+24, d_clock=ceil(n/2)+32, B_clock=2^d_clock, exact score arithmetic from Appendix A and QFT precision from Sections 2 and 6. For N=2 use the fixed-size exact endpoint branch without the coarse selector. For every adaptive adversary allowed by claim 5, including the clean input, it returns the whole s with unconditional probability at least 11/16>2/3. All four bounds hold jointly on every execution branch, including either selector cap and an unfinished probe, with constants independent of N, s, the adversary and outcomes. Worst-case total charged sequential work is T=O(2^(n/2)n^(18/5)), including all classical bit operations, source acquisition, circuit generation and literal inversion, gates, measurements, initialization, certified QFT-word synthesis, controller boundaries and indexed addresses. The full representative envelope B_T(n)=2^(n/2)n^(18/5) has exact growth index 1.

For every N >= 2 and s in Z/NZ, put n=ceil(log2 N). The same single bank-first clock algorithm in proof.md and critical_third_adaptive_clock_selector.md, with the parameter rule in claims 1-4, guarantees fractional tolerance epsilon(n)=1/3 under exactly the adaptive delivery model in error_model, with no validity threshold. All Q raw copies arrive before any algorithm measurement, private random draw or source transformation. The permitted malformed count is floor(Q/3)=Q/3. Lemma 0 proves that every allowed adversary induces a convex mixture of fixed clean-product/bad-block bank inputs. For every such adversary, including the clean input, full-secret success is at least 11/16>2/3. On every execution branch the same algorithm jointly satisfies T=O(2^(n/2)n^(18/5)), S_C=O(n), S_Q=O(n^2), and the exact Q rule above. Constants are independent of N, s, the adversary and outcomes. This fraction bounds the count among all acquired copies, not a per-copy corruption probability.

structured.error_model: Adaptive malformed-copy model with fraction epsilon(n). Parameters: N >= 2 is the modulus, s in Z/NZ the secret, n = ceil(log2 N), Q the total number of source copies the algorithm acquires, and epsilon(n) the tolerated malformed fraction. Copies are delivered one at a time in acquisition order j = 1, ..., Q. Before copy j is delivered, an adversary that knows N, s, the full description of the algorithm, and every measurement outcome the algorithm obtained before copy j is delivered, and that may hold, process and measure an arbitrary private quantum system, decides adaptively whether copy j is malformed; on every execution branch at most floor(epsilon(n) Q) of the Q acquired copies are malformed. A malformed copy is an arbitrary (n+1)-qubit state (the register shape of an ideal copy) supplied from the adversary's system: it may be pure or mixed, may be entangled with the adversary's remaining system and with other malformed copies, and may depend on all of the information above; it is not entangled with clean copies or with the algorithm's workspace, ancillas or internal random bits. Every copy that is not malformed is clean: at the moment of its delivery, a fresh ideal coset state rho_s = (1/N) sum_x |psi_{x,s}><psi_{x,s}| in tensor product with everything else (the adversary's system, all other copies and the algorithm's workspace), i.e. clean copies are independent ideal coset states. The adversary interacts with the algorithm only by supplying copies; after delivery it has no access to the copy or to the algorithm's quantum or classical systems. All measurements have countably many outcomes. The algorithm is not told which copies are malformed. Quantifiers: the guarantee must hold for every N >= 2 (no validity threshold), every s in Z/NZ and every such adversary, including the adversary that corrupts nothing (the clean problem): the algorithm outputs the entire s with probability at least 2/3, and the four declared resource bounds hold on every execution branch. The fraction bounds the number of malformed copies among acquired copies; it is not a per-copy corruption probability.
